# M1 implementation and verification

**Status: M1 is closed (2026-10-24) for the operator-accepted single-host Fedora x86_64 / RTX 5090 deployment.** Locked restore, a clean Release warnings-as-errors build and all **1,750 deterministic tests** pass. The current-M1 privileged systemd workflow passed against the corrected, checksum-verified binaries, including the original five-second polling target and verified cleanup. Separate-LAN qualification is explicitly deferred by the operator; it is not passing evidence. The [M1 plan](M1-ingest-and-search.md) and [accepted topology exception in spec §17](../../spec.md#17-non-functional-requirements) define this closure.

## M1 closure (2026-10-24)

- **Scope decision:** the operator confirmed that no second machine is available and explicitly accepted single-host scope. Separate-LAN qualification is deferred, not counted as passing. Its required hardware, all-role readiness and ingestion evidence remain in the [operator procedure](../../deploy/tests/m1-live-LAN-handoff.md). All other M1 targets remain required.
- **Polling correction:** two actual systemd runs missed the five-second polling gate ([first run](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/systemd-first-attempt.log), [diagnostic run](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/systemd-second-attempt.log)). A fixed 250 ms scheduler sleep could cross a source's next deadline. The loop now sleeps only until the earliest active-source deadline or the 250 ms event backstop, whichever comes first. Disabled/removed sources do not contribute deadlines. The [clock-controlled regression](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/poll-regression-results.json) fails before the correction and passes afterward. Timing assertions retain their original limits and now print diagnostics; fixture cleanup also clears its own failed-unit state and reports completion.
- **Final source checks:** locked restore, a full Release rebuild with zero warnings/errors, and **1,750 passed / zero failed / zero skipped** ([counts](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/final-deterministic-results.json), [build](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/final-build.log), [tests](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/final-tests.log)). The additional test is `PollingSourceWakesAtDeadlineAfterLateSchedulerTick`.
- **Vector qualification:** the separate [million-vector test](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/vector-scale-results.json) passed with 100,000 replacements, 4,294,967,296 vector bytes and no retained-slot growth. This is component evidence; the full deployed scale measurements below remain the October 9 runs.
- **Fresh operator bundle:** all 416 files were checksummed, all 19 package locks remain unchanged, and the [publish provenance](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/final-publish-provenance.json) binds the bundle to the corrected runtime sources. The [qualification-input hashes](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/qualification-input-sha256.json) identify the workflow, units fixture and regression inputs. The installed M0 service is unchanged.
- **Final systemd workflow: passed.** The operator ran `artifacts/m1-qualification/operator-publish-20261024-poll-deadline/merged` through the shipped isolated harness. Keyword/vector capture took **0.395/0.403 s**, inbox PDF visibility **12.732 s**, event edit visibility **1.812 s**, and polling visibility **4.929 s after rsync commit** against the unchanged **5 s** limit (**4.993 s including rsync**). Text/PDF/crafted-PDF, structured query, move identity, suppression/restore, interrupted-work restart, rebuild text/chunk equality and jobs all passed ([results](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/systemd-final-results.json), [full log](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/systemd-final.log)).
- **Live profile and teardown: passed.** All provider roles and the extractor reported ready while the canary was blocked; all **416 deployed file hashes** matched the fresh bundle. The daemon used UID 1654, no capabilities, strict filesystem protection and an 8 GiB/256-task limit; the extractor used UID 1655, a private network, inaccessible stores/secrets and a 1 GiB/64-task limit ([observation](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/systemd-final-observation.json)). All final-fixture paths and units were removed and port 17171 closed. The installed M0 service remains active with its original October 9 start time ([cleanup](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/systemd-final-cleanup.json)).
- **Durable evidence:** the [artifact manifest](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/artifact-manifest.json) records the current results, failed attempts, source/binary provenance and [18-gate test audit](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/gate-test-audit.json). October 9 evidence remains separate and unmodified.

The October 9 sections below retain the original qualification evidence and its then-open gates. The scheduler correction does not change extraction, retrieval, vector storage or the scale algorithms. The earlier independent source review did not review this new correction.

Implementation and closure corrections were performed by GPT-6.1 Sol agents after the earlier review, retaining the seven original Daybreak security fixes implemented by Opus. Later Sol changes received independent native standards/specification reviews, parent integration review and targeted regressions; this does not claim a new Daybreak review of the latest changes. The installed M0 daemon has not been changed. M0 remains closed for its accepted Fedora x86_64/Tailscale scope; its explicit remote-CI, Access, macOS, arm64 and certificate follow-ups remain deferred under that closure record.

## Closure implementation corrections

The latest corrections retain safe source globs, durable per-entry rejection without host failure, admission-budget ordering before coalesced read-only accounting, unavailable-document plaintext filtering, purge override/cache-owner cleanup and durable cleanup markers from the seven Daybreak fixes.

Sol's follow-up changes include reload-aware step-up authorization; A→B→A embedding-space activation and avoiding idle corpus reloads; fenced dirty-document vector refresh; same-byte move preservation of extraction metadata and locators; replacement-tag overrides; `indexed_partial` on edits; exhaustive malformed-filter validation before provider calls; FLD-6 durable candidate plans and bounded missing-to-removed reconciliation; four persistent file workers and immediate stale-lease recovery under the data-root lock; per-parser 120-second CPU limits; terminal named-bound `skipped` outcomes; external source paths for index-mode retrieval; daemon-owned sticky `1770` inbox and private `0700` claims pinned and validated through the same descriptor; atomic fenced cache restoration during rebuild with completed matching jobs; SQL child/input-hash indexes; and real PDF page-marker mapping to chunk locators.

Targeted regressions include `SecondAbsentScanExpiresMoveWindowButSamePathReattachesRetainedIdentity`, `SameByteMovePreservesExtractionMetadataAndPageLocators`, `ChangedStagedMoveBytesDoNotOverwriteTheEnumeratedHashIdentity`, `InvalidSemanticFiltersAreRejectedBeforeProviderWork`, `ExtractionDeadlineIsDurableNamedBoundAndIsNotRetried`, `FileQueueUsesFourBoundedWorkersAndDrainsWithoutPerFilePollingDelay`, `RestartImmediatelyReclaimsUnexpiredExtractionLeaseWithoutDuplicateAdmission`, `RebuildRestoresCachedVectorsAndOwnersWithoutPendingProviderWork`, `CacheRestorationUsesInputHashIndexAcrossSpaces`, and `DistinctIdentityStagingTests`. The final integrated 1,749-test run passed, including exact contribution-state and bounded-maintenance regressions. Earlier source-freeze and targeted results remain recorded separately.

## Implemented paths

- JSON and multipart capture; durable, credential-attributed admission, reservations, jobs and leases; idempotency binds content, metadata and file-format hint.
- Folder events/debounce/polling/deep rescans, built-in inbox claims, conservative moves, absence and suppression, source disable/removal, and durable import-candidate checkpoints.
- Descriptor-based Markdown, text, PDF, HTML and DOCX extraction in a supervised sandbox; bounded streamed output, private staging, original-file preservation and extraction-cache reuse. Unsupported/OCR-required/error results remain explicit.
- Lossless text and NFC search normalization with offset maps. FTS indexes each chunk's slice of the normalized search text, and highlight ranges map back to the lossless chunk through the offset map. Chunks preserve heading context and bounded code/table blocks; parsed tags/links and source times; original properties and durable user overrides.
- Chunk bounds (512 target, 1,024 maximum, 64 overlap) are budgeted in **UTF-8 bytes, not model tokens**. A byte-fallback tokenizer never emits more tokens than input bytes, so the byte budget is a conservative token bound for any embedding model without loading its tokenizer. The cost is smaller chunks than a token budget would allow for non-ASCII text.
- Transactional text/chunk/FTS/metadata projections, normalized SQLite vectors, dense segmented slots, startup preload, committed-generation invalidation, cached embedding reuse, and authoritative-generation-fenced embedding-space activation.
- Keyword, semantic and hybrid retrieval; SQL-prefiltered document candidates, exact SIMD scoring, three-chunk diversity per leg, RRF, recency boost, optional LLM/provider reranking, and explicit degradation. FTS phrases/prefixes and highlights use actual match positions. The configurable exact cap defaults to one million chunks.
- Bounded same-revision neighbor expansion for context consumers. Query cursors are bound to the instance (`meta.instance_id`), the `query` operation, the query hash, sort position, processing generation and credential authority. Opt-in, body-free traces are capped at 200 with purge lineage.
- Managed create/edit/trash/restore/purge through journaled filesystem effects, conflict preservation as `<name>.conflict-<timestamp>.md`, crash recovery, late-job fencing and payload/cache/trace redaction. API-key non-additive mutations create proposals, including a tag set that drops any current tag; only a superset of the current tags executes directly. Execution/approval is M2.
- Capture admission (capacity and queued jobs) runs before the original is written to the vault; a capacity rejection leaves no managed file and no journal entry.
- Startup sweeps stale staging files. Only owned, single-link regular files with the stager's own names are removed; symlinks are never followed, and directories and other entries are kept.
- Folder scans report entries that exist but cannot be opened, stat'd or hashed as unreadable. Unreadable entries, and anything beneath them, are neither imported nor marked `missing`.
- HTTP/OpenAPI contracts, original-file downloads, revision checks, job retry/source/maintenance routes, and `brain add`, `brain search`, `brain query` with JSON output.

M2 assistant execution, M3 UI, and M4 parser/enrichment/budget/retention features remain outside this implementation. Neighbor expansion is a repository context-pack operation; it does not silently add unranked neighbors to `/search` results.

dotnet restore SecondBrain.slnx --locked-mode --disable-build-servers -m:1

## Historical retrieval scale diagnostics

An earlier diagnostic used 100,000 documents, one million 1024-dimensional vectors, and twenty warm requests per mode/filter combination. The type filter selects 100,000 chunks; all chunks contain the same query term and have identical unit vectors. This deliberately exercises broad lexical matching and deterministic ties. Provider time is zero. It runs the production repository in a standalone test process on this host's temporary filesystem, not the complete Docker daemon on NVMe, so it supplements rather than replaces reference-deployment qualification.

| Mode | Filtered 100k chunks p95 | Unfiltered 1M chunks p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Keyword | 507.483 ms | 1,029.912 ms |
| Semantic | 42.920 ms | 420.129 ms |
| Hybrid | **562.254 ms** | **1,440.853 ms** |

Structured query p95 was **6.366 ms** in the earlier diagnostic, but the old empty-generation structured-query fixture is not valid current acceptance evidence. **The historical hybrid measurements missed both targets.** Later fixes changed loading, SQL bounds and scoring; these historical misses remain diagnostic history and neither establish current failure nor current acceptance. The final deployed post-consolidation metrics below supersede these historical diagnostics.

Cold vector load plus first hybrid search took 12.841 seconds. End-of-run managed memory was 4,505,067,312 bytes and working set 4,782,092,288 bytes; these are sampled process values, not peak daemon-plus-sandbox measurements. Seeding took 12.120 seconds.

The measurements exposed and fixed a five-second SQLite statement timeout during monolithic vector loading. Loading now pages sparse row IDs in a single committed snapshot, restores per-document ordinal order, and preloads before readiness. A growing SQL top-k prefix avoids a full lexical result sort while preserving filters, ties and document diversity. Vector scoring avoids unnecessary candidate allocations and per-vector monitor acquisition. Broad-match BM25 and joins dominated that earlier diagnostic. Current acceptance depends on the final deployed full-scale results, not extrapolation from this run.

## Final authoritative deployment measurements

The final server image `sha256:a779863aacae340af5f64aafe9b84773d258fb213263ec75a1c96f082fa31552` ran against 100,000 authoritative documents and 1,000,000 recorded 1,024-dimensional vectors on the NVMe reference-size host. The actual rebuild completed in **1,556.694 seconds** (25.945 minutes), made **zero embedding requests**, and preserved all durable text, chunks, vectors, cache owners, document revisions and chunk/page locators. The first immediate post-rebuild hybrid query succeeded in **9.416 seconds HTTP / 9,381.954 ms repository**, including the dirty registry refresh under the unchanged 15-second lease.

The retained pre-maintenance segmented index still missed warm latency (185.25/406.33 ms). After genuine bounded consolidation, the separate final profile validated all **96 result fingerprints** and **64 warm cache-hit requests**: provider-excluded repository p95 **45.279 ms filtered** and **313.792 ms unfiltered**, structured HTTP p95 **40.618 ms**. These are warm measurements; cold contribution fill and first post-rebuild costs remain separately recorded. Retained derived lexical state was **223,093,210 bytes**, peak **223,617,498 bytes**, below the combined 384 MiB cap; this caches exact native primitive contributions rather than answers.

Process-to-health was **13.637 seconds**, including actual startup vector preload **10.865 seconds**, satisfying `<3 seconds + vector load`. Managed heap above the logical live vector payload was **721,107,488 bytes** (above the allocated live vector array: **522,140,192 bytes**), below the 1 GB allowance. Four concurrent 80-page sandbox PDFs plus queries remained healthy. Combined daemon/sandbox sampled cgroup peak was **6,006,628,352 bytes**; the sum of separate lifetime peaks provides a conservative **6,307,229,696-byte** upper bound. One-second sampling can miss short peaks, so both measures are retained. The shipped daemon limit is finite 8 GiB and extractor limits remain enforced.

The fixture repeats the recorded seed topics to establish scale equivalence and resource bounds. It does not create an independent 100k-document relevance evaluation, real inference latency or separate-host LAN topology; those distinctions remain explicit in the artifacts. The original seed accidentally loaded an older Debug qualification assembly; its actual assembly hashes and fixture originals `0644`/vault directories `0755` beneath the private `0700` data root are preserved as fixture provenance, not attributed to the final source. Final runtime image and packaged qualification assembly hashes are recorded separately. The final rebuild and all post-consolidation measurements used the reviewed production image.

Source re-extraction preserves authored overrides/raw properties. Current deployed 640-document rehearsal rebuilt in **10.809 seconds** with zero provider calls and text/chunk/locator equality; the final authoritative 100k-document rebuild passes in **1,556.694 seconds**, with zero provider calls and exhaustive equality. |

[Supplemental deployed overlap](evidence/m1-closure-20261009/live-publication-throughput.json) resolves revisions, metadata and chunk text/context/pages during actual live ingestion: 19 Markdown and 16 PDF same-running-job overlap samples. This observes ingestion overlap, not the exact commit instant. |

## Earlier code-review fixes (2026-10-09)

This table preserves the earlier implementation history; the closure corrections above supersede its original open-ended absence behavior. Each fix has a regression test except the documentation and structural items, which the architecture and composition tests guard.

| Item | Fix | Proving test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1, absence vs read error (U17) | `SourceFileEntry.Unreadable` reports entries that exist but cannot be opened, stat'd or hashed. Only `ENOENT` or a symlink (`ELOOP`) is treated as not present. The planner neither imports nor marks unreadable paths, or anything beneath them, `missing`. | `UnreadableEntriesAreReportedRatherThanOmitted` (Extractor.Tests), `UnreadableEntriesStayIndexedAndAreNeverMarkedAbsent` (Storage.Tests) |
| A2, admission before vault write (ING-4) | `IPublicationCoordinator.CheckAdmissionAsync` runs the same capacity/queued-job query before capture, file and folder admissions write the original. If publication still rejects a fresh document, `DiscardUnpublishedImportAsync` removes the file and its journal rows. | `CapacityRejectionLeavesNoManagedOriginalOrJournalEntry`, `UnpublishedImportIsDiscardedButPublishedOriginalIsKept` |
| A3, stale staging cleanup | `InputStager.CleanStaleAsync` (Core port `IStagingRecovery`) runs in `StorageStartupService` after journal and publication recovery. | `StartupSweepRemovesOnlyOwnedRegularStagedFiles` |
| A4, conflict name | `<name>.conflict-<timestamp>.md` with the 100 ns prepare timestamp and no hash suffix. Mutations on one destination are serialized by its reservation. | `JournalTests.ConflictKeepsExternalEditAndRecordsItsNewRevision` (exact-name regex) |
| A5, move window (U9) | A move matches an absence that is still open (document `missing`, absence uncleared) instead of one recorded within 2 minutes of wall-clock time. | `MoveAdmittedLongAfterTheAbsenceKeepsIdentityWhileTheAbsenceIsOpen` |
| A6, tag removal | A tags array is the requested set. A key may execute only a superset of the current tags directly; dropping any tag is a proposal. Sessions replace the set. | `TagAdditionsExecuteDirectlyButTagRemovalFromAKeyIsAProposal` |
| A7, FTS over search text | `TextProcessor.Process` builds chunks from the lossless text. FTS now indexes each chunk's normalized search slice, and highlights map back through `offset_map`. `chunks.text` stays lossless. | `FtsSearchesTheNormalizedTextAndHighlightsMapToLosslessOffsets` |
| A8, cursor binding | The query cursor carries and checks `meta.instance_id` and the `query` operation. | `QueryCursorRejectsAnotherOperationOrInstance` |
| A9, deep rescan schedule (FLD-2) | Appendix B `ingest.deep_rescan_at` (default `"03:00"`, in `time.zone`) is validated and drives `DeepRescanSchedule.Next`. The loader now keeps the modeled `ingest` keys, so `sync_embed_deadline_ms` is also honored from YAML. | `DeepRescanScheduleTests`, `DeepRescanTimeDefaultsToNightlyAndIsConfigurable`, `DeepRescanTimeMustBeATwentyFourHourTime` |
| A10, status vocabulary | The persisted and API-visible status is `missing`. `DocumentStatusNames` (Core) and `DocumentStatusSql` (Storage) hold the unavailable-status set once. | Folder absence tests assert `missing` |
| A11, chunk bounds | Documentation only: the plan and this report state the UTF-8 byte bound and why. | — |

The result DTO lives once in BCL-only `SecondBrain.Extraction.Contracts`, used directly by Core's `IExtractorClient` port, the sandbox and Infrastructure. ## Remaining qualification and handoff

M1 is closed within the accepted scope recorded above. Source enumeration remains bounded at 500,000 entries; durable import candidates and reconciliation metadata survive restart. FLD-6 expires prior missing occurrences only after the next complete reconciliation plan drains, preserving conservative move matching within that window. Query/publication share a consistency gate, and committed vector deltas refresh in bounded batches.

- **Full-scale targets:** the October 9 authoritative 100k-document/1M-chunk deployment passed locally. Those measurements remain dated evidence; the October 24 change affects poll scheduling, not the extraction, retrieval, vector-storage or scale algorithms.
- **Current-M1 systemd qualification:** passed on October 24, including the corrected polling deadline, real model roles, hardening observations, matching deployed binaries and teardown. The installed M0 daemon was not replaced.
- **Evidence:** the [October 24 manifest](evidence/m1-closure-20261024/artifact-manifest.json) supplements the immutable [October 9 manifest](evidence/m1-closure-20261009/artifact-manifest.json). Host SDK 10.0.111 and Docker SDK 10.0.105 remain distinct; no claim of byte-identical assemblies across those builds is made.

| Follow-up | Status and completion evidence |

Use the [separate-LAN procedure](../../deploy/tests/m1-live-LAN-handoff.md) to record two distinct machines, the RTX 5090/provider configuration, all-role readiness, live ingestion/latency results and provider timing. Same-host results do not establish this topology. This deferral changes M1 acceptance only; later milestone requirements remain unchanged. |

## M1-to-M2 planning handoff

This handoff is planning only; M1 is closed within its explicitly accepted scope, and no M2 runtime behavior is claimed. M2 should consume M1's application services for filtered retrieval, structured queries, committed metadata/text/vector snapshots, generation-bound chunk/page locators, bounded neighbor expansion, credential-bound cursors and explicit degraded reasons. Durable proposal records, payload lineage, publication fences and the mutation journal provide the seams for interactive approval and exactly-once execution; assistant turns, citation verification, exposure limits, conversation ownership, SSE replay and MCP authorization remain M2 work under spec §19.

Use the recorded M1 gate evidence and retain the explicit separate-LAN follow-up. Preserve the existing shared payload/reference store, current authority/privacy checks and purge lineage when adding assistant execution. M2 still needs its own implementation and acceptance evidence; M1 closure does not establish assistant or MCP behavior.
